summary: Records IANA's allocation of a block of Diameter command codes to the Third Generation Partnership Project for its Release 5. It takes no position on how they are used, and the codes cannot be reused for later releases. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo records a block of Diameter command codes assigned for 3GPP Release 5. It says the codes are for that release and not general-purpose mechanisms.

questions: can 3gpp release 5 diameter codes be reused
which diameter codes were allocated for 3gpp release 5
subtitle: Diameter command code allocation for 3GPP Release 5 applications.

tldr.problem: 3GPP Release 5 Diameter applications for the Internet Multimedia Subsystem needed new command codes.
tldr.mechanism: The memo records IANA's allocation of Diameter command codes 300 through 313 for 3GPP Release 5.
tldr.outcome: The codes are for Release 5 only; the RFC says they cannot be reused for future releases and notes that the protocols were not carefully reviewed by the IETF.

today: RFC 3589 is an Informational allocation memo for 3GPP Release 5 Diameter command codes. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: Why 3GPP Needed Codes
sections.content:
3GPP was defining an Internet Multimedia Subsystem as part of its Release 5 architecture. The architecture included a Diameter application that needed new command codes.

This RFC documents the allocation and does not judge how the codes are used. It identifies the application as specific to Release 5.
sections.plainLanguage: A 3GPP application needed new command numbers for Release 5. This memo records the allocation without evaluating the application.

sections.title: Codes 300 Through 313
sections.content:
IANA allocated Diameter command codes 300 through 313 for use in 3GPP Release 5. The RFC says the associated protocols had not been carefully reviewed by the IETF and were not considered general mechanisms for broad use.

The memo says future releases cannot reuse these codes and are expected to use alternate mechanisms. It anticipates that codes for Release 6 would come from standard command space with IETF documentation.
sections.plainLanguage: The allocated range is reserved for Release 5. The memo says later releases need other mechanisms and standard allocation procedures.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says it is not known to affect Internet security. It allocates command-code values but does not define their protocol behavior.

The application details are referenced in 3GPP specifications. This memo's role is limited to documenting the codes and their intended release.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo says the allocation has no known effect on Internet security. It does not specify how the commands work.
